# Jamaican Curry Chicken over Rice & Peas 🇯🇲

::: {.dish-meta}
**Region:** Jamaica (Caribbean)  ·  **Family:** Curry + coconut rice, served over
**Serves:** 4–6  ·  **Active time:** 50 minutes  ·  **Total:** 1 hour 30 min
**Assembly:** 🍚 Chicken over rice — curry ladled over coconut cowpea rice
:::

Golden, allspice-scented curry chicken with soft potato and a rich gravy, spooned
over a mound of **rice and peas** — long-grain rice simmered in coconut milk with
cowpeas, thyme, and a whole Scotch bonnet. It's the Jamaican Sunday plate, and
arguably the island's national comfort food.

## The story

Curry came to Jamaica with **indentured laborers from India** in the 19th century,
after the abolition of slavery, and the island made it thoroughly its own.
**Jamaican curry powder** is turmeric-gold and leans on locally beloved
**allspice** (*pimento*), while the cooking picks up the Scotch bonnet heat and
thyme-and-scallion backbone of Jamaican kitchens.

Its constant companion is **rice and peas** — where "peas" means beans. The dish
predates the modern kidney-bean version: rural and old-time cooks made it with
**cowpeas** (and *gungo*, or pigeon peas, at Christmas), simmered with the rice in
coconut milk. The two are cooked separately and married on the plate, the curry
gravy sinking into the coconut rice.

## Ingredients

**Curry chicken**

- 1 kg (2.2 lb) bone-in chicken, cut into large pieces
- 3 tbsp Jamaican curry powder (turmeric- and allspice-forward)
- 4 cloves garlic, minced; 1 tbsp grated ginger
- 1 onion, diced; 3 scallions, chopped; 3 sprigs thyme
- 1 tsp ground allspice (pimento), or 6 whole berries
- 1 Scotch bonnet, left **whole and unbroken**
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (or coconut oil)
- 2 waxy potatoes, cut into chunks
- ~350 ml (1.5 cups) chicken stock or water; salt & black pepper

**Rice & peas (coconut cowpea rice)**

- 200 g (1 cup) dried cowpeas, soaked overnight (or 1½ cans, drained)
- 400 ml (1 can) coconut milk
- 300 g (1.5 cups) long-grain rice, rinsed
- 3 cloves garlic; 2 scallions, smashed; 3 sprigs thyme
- 1 Scotch bonnet, whole; ½ tsp ground allspice; salt
- Water as needed

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Gluten-free · dairy-free:** naturally both — the richness is coconut milk, not
dairy, and nothing here is breaded or floured. Just use a **gluten-free curry
powder** (most are, but check) and **don't thicken the gravy with flour** — reduce
it, or mash a little of the potato in instead.
:::

## Method

### Curry the chicken

1. Toss the chicken with the curry powder, garlic, ginger, half the scallions,
   thyme, allspice, salt, and pepper. Marinate at least 30 minutes (overnight is
   better).
2. **Bloom the curry:** heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium. Scrape any loose
   curry paste off the chicken into the oil and fry 1 minute until fragrant and
   darkened (this "burns" the curry, Jamaican-style, and deepens the color).
3. Add the chicken and sear on all sides, 6–8 minutes, letting a brown fond build.
   Add the onion and remaining scallions and cook 3 minutes.
4. Pour in the stock, add the **whole Scotch bonnet**, and bring to a simmer.
   Cover and cook 25 minutes.
5. Add the potatoes and simmer, uncovered, another 15–20 minutes until the chicken
   is tender and the gravy has reduced and thickened. Fish out the Scotch bonnet
   (whole) and thyme stems. Taste for salt.

### Rice & peas

6. If using dried cowpeas, simmer the soaked peas in fresh water until just tender,
   30–40 minutes; drain, saving the liquid. (Canned: skip to step 7.)
7. In a pot, combine the cowpeas, coconut milk, garlic, scallions, thyme, whole
   Scotch bonnet, and allspice. Add water (or bean liquid) to reach **1.5× the
   volume of the rice**. Season with salt and bring to a boil.
8. Stir in the rinsed rice, return to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest
   heat 20 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Rest, covered, 10 minutes.
   Remove the Scotch bonnet and thyme; fluff.

### Serve

9. Mound the rice and peas on each plate and **ladle the curry chicken and its
   gravy over the top**, so it soaks in. Serve with fried plantain, a simple
   cabbage slaw, and extra Scotch bonnet pepper sauce for the brave.

## The whole-pepper trick

Both pots use a **whole, unbroken Scotch bonnet** — it perfumes the chicken and the
rice with fruity heat without setting the whole dish on fire. Just don't let it
burst, and warn whoever finds it on their plate. Pierce it if you want real island
heat throughout.

## Make it yours

- **The peas:** cowpeas are the old-time choice, but **red kidney beans** are the
  everyday standard and **gungo (pigeon) peas** are the Christmas special — all are
  correct.
- **Coconut depth:** for richer rice and peas, use the thick cream from the top of
  the can and reduce the added water.
- Add a stick of cinnamon or a few pimento berries to the rice for a more festive
  version.
- Leftover curry gravy over rice the next day is, quietly, the best part.
